==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
Borrowed from {{bor|en|fr|escorte}}, itself borrowed from {{der|en|it|scorta}}.

===Pronunciation===
*Noun:
** {{IPA|en|/ˈɛs.kɔɹt/|a=GA}}
*** {{audio|en|En-us-escort.ogg|a=US}}
** {{IPA|en|/ˈɛs.kɔːt/|a=RP}}
** {{hyph|en|es|cort}}
*Verb:
** {{IPA|en|/ɪsˈkɔɹt/|a=GA}}
** {{IPA|en|/ɪsˈkɔːt/|a=RP}}
*** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-escort (verb).wav|a=Southern England}}
** {{hyph|en|es|cort}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɔː(ɹ)t|s=2}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A [[group]] of [[people]] or [[vehicle]]s, generally [[armed]], who go with a [[person]] or people of [[importance]] to [[safeguard]] them on a [[journey]] or [[mission]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1898|author=w:Arnold Henry Savage Landor|title=In the Forbidden Land|chapter=LXXXIII
|passage=The soldier who was pulling at the other end was clumsily unhorsed, and I myself was all but thrown by the unexpected jerk. This ludicrous incident at first provoked mirth among my '''escort''', a mirth which their superstitious minds immediately turned into an ill omen.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1883|author=w:Ambrose Bierce|title=George Thurston
|passage=Whole squadrons of cavalry '''escort''' had sometimes to be sent thundering against a powerful infantry outpost in order that the brief time between the charge and the inevitable retreat might be utilized in sounding a ford or determining the point of intersection of two roads.}}
# An accompanying person in such a group.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1980|author=Ernest L. Secrest|title=My 1102 Days of W.W. II|chapter=9|passage=The waves being so high when we and the '''escorts''', which stayed about one quarter mile to each side and ahead of us, were in a trough at the same time and we were unable to see one another.}}
# A guard who travels with a dangerous person, such as a criminal, for the protection of others.
# A group of people attending as a mark of respect or honor.
# An accompanying person in a social gathering, etc.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1921|author=w:Mary Roberts Rinehart|title=More Tish|chapter=5|passage="He'd come in for something to eat—the red-bearded one. We had quite a chat. I told him we were traveling like Stevenson—with a donkey; but that one of the ladies had an abscess on a tooth and was going home. He said it was no place for women and offered himself as an '''escort'''."}}
# Protection, care, or safeguard on a journey or excursion.
# {{lb|en|originally|euphemistic}} A [[sex worker]] who does not operate in a [[brothel]], but with whom clients make [[appointment]]s; a [[call girl]] or male equivalent; a [[pimp]].

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# To attend to in order to guard and protect; to accompany as a [[safeguard]] (for the person escorted or for others); to give honorable or ceremonious attendance to.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2009|author=Allen D. Grimshaw|title=A Social History of Racial Violence
|passage=He reported that the police '''escorted''' the children five or six blocks beyond Natural Bridge Avenue and at that point stopped the white children who were following and shooed them back to the park.}}
# To accompany (a person) in order to compel them to go somewhere (e.g. to leave a building).
# To go with someone as a [[partner]], for example on a formal [[date]].
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To work as an escort (sex worker).
